comments.content:
Hi Emmanuel,

I ran the check you suggested: on my grouped OOF our twin-LoRA blend (no external members) gets 0.633 alone, and adding your mistral7b on top gets 0.645 (+0.012 at w=1.0; +0.014 at w=1.5); olmo2_7b alone gives +0.002; greedy over {blend, mistral7b, olmo2_7b} lands on 0.6475. So your members do add real signal on our side — not the flashiest jump, but consistent.

I'd like to explore a merge if you're still open. Our stack on its own scores 0.682 on the public board (fork of the current public 0.682) with a k=2-realistic validation harness, and we don't carry Mistral or OLMo — the gap is genuinely missing for us.

I can publish our OOF as a public dataset this week so you can run the same mutual check you offered to Antonin. Let me know if that helps moved things forward.

Is the team still looking for one more?

  • Folds: sklearn GroupKFold(n_splits=5) on prompt_id over train.csv in file order. Each row has its fold in the "fold" column, so you can re-map to your own split if yours differs.

Hi! I'm Emmanuel (public 0.663). I'd like to propose a team merge for Name That LLM.

What I'd bring:

  • Two LoRA members no public notebook uses: Mistral-7B and OLMo-2-7B two-stage, trained on an expanded pool, with full 5-fold OOF predictions on all 2,699 train rows (0.60 balanced accuracy, leak-free). You can weight them against your stack straight away.
  • A per-pair error map of the weak classes (claude-fable-5 vs glm-5.3, glm-5.3 vs flash, gpt-5.6-sol vs luna, gemini 3.7 vs 3.8 flash) and what did and didn't work on them.
  • Fresh Gemini flash passages I'm generating now for the Gemini confusions.
  • Spare GPU hours every week for training runs you don't have time for.

I'm happy to take on whatever experiments you need. Open to a quick chat? Reply here or send a merge request to team "Emmanuel Ocheme".

Emmanuel
